assumptions: The venture will not itself perform reserved legal, payment, or regulated collection activities without the required authorization.
Licensed recovery partners will permit compliant outcome tracking and success-fee settlement if agreements can be reached.
No unreported creditor mandates, accountant partnerships, recovery results, or willingness-to-pay evidence exists.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A legal-scope opinion and compliant mandate/payment design, signed agreements with at least one licensed recovery partner and one repeatable accountant channel, plus a prospective cohort segmented by claim quality showing recovery uplift, time to cash, partner costs, complaint and dispute rates, customer retention, net contribution, and repeat portfolio submission.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Charging only on cleared recovery aligns incentives around an observable cash event, while routing claims to progressively stronger actions could preserve debtor relationships better than uniform collection. The insight is credible but not uniquely proprietary.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Late invoices impose direct liquidity and administrative costs, giving SMEs an economically important problem and a natural budget source in recovered proceeds. Willingness to surrender 8-15% and authorize action remains untested, especially where customer relationships matter.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Success fees provide strong buyer alignment and cash is collected from realized outcomes, but revenue arrives only on successful recoveries. Recovery rates, claim quality, partner shares, case-support burden, CAC, repeat volume, compliance overhead, and the scale projection are all unvalidated; adverse selection could compress contribution margins.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish micro and small B2B creditors are a large pain-defined segment, and overdue invoices provide a clear trigger. The beachhead needs further narrowing by invoice size, age, dispute status, and industry to make routing and economics repeatable.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Neutral multi-route orchestration could differentiate the offer, but collection agencies, law firms, factoring providers, accounting platforms, and software vendors already occupy relevant workflows. With no mandates, exclusive supply, or channel agreements, a dominant position is speculative.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Successful recovery data and customer access could support monitoring, credit scoring, payment automation, mediation, insurance, financing referrals, and geographic or sector expansion. Regulatory scope and trust requirements constrain how quickly these adjacencies can be captured.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Outcome data could improve route selection and workflow embedding could create switching costs, but those advantages require substantial proprietary volume. Partners may retain key outcome data, accountants can refer elsewhere, and incumbents can imitate routing and outcome pricing.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: One intake point, relationship-sensitive escalation, and payment only on recovery are meaningful conveniences. There is no comparative evidence yet that the marketplace recovers more, faster, more cheaply, or with less relationship damage than direct engagement with existing providers.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Persistent SME late-payment pressure and increasingly automatable document intake and case triage support the concept. The evidence does not show a temporary regulatory or channel opening that gives this entrant unusual momentum.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Accountants and bookkeeping platforms are logically placed referral channels with recurring access to invoice workflows, but every proposed agreement is unsigned and the founder has no existing channel rights. Direct diagnostics provide a fallback, though likely with weaker economics and more sales effort.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: Software intake and scoring fit the founder, and licensed partners can execute regulated steps, but legal boundaries, mandates, complaints, payments, disputes, reputational harm, and partner quality require specialized oversight. The marketplace also has a two-sided launch problem and may exceed a comfortable part-time operating load.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure a bookkeeping-platform or accountant-network integration that supplies permissioned, prequalified overdue invoices under a standardized mandate, while keeping regulated execution and fund handling with licensed partners and retaining portable outcome data.
main_structural_strength: The offer attaches pricing to a severe, measurable customer outcome—cash actually recovered—creating clear incentive alignment and a broad base for repeat transaction volume and data-driven routing.
primary_score_limiter: The proposed control point is not controlled: creditor mandates, accountant distribution, licensed execution, payment mechanics, and outcome-data rights are all unsigned or unknown.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The supplied contrary evidence indicates that SMEs may avoid collection to protect commercial relationships, while regulated legal and payment activities require qualified partners, directly weakening conversion and operational control.
